reason: While the text depicts Hamor (the leader) and Shechem proposing a collaborative arrangement to the men of the city, and the townspeople initially agreeing to be circumcised, this apparent cooperation is built entirely on deception. Jacob's sons agree under false pretenses with the intent to betray. The narrative culminates in violent slaughter and plunder of the city by Simeon and Levi, followed by Jacob's rebuke of their actions. The text portrays deceit, violence, and tribal conflict rather than genuine leaders and people working together constructively. Any collaboration shown is superficial and is destroyed by treachery.
